metadata.title: GAM-001: CRISPR-Cas9 sgRNA Design and Cloning
metadata.purpose: Design CRISPR-Cas9 sgRNAs, clone the selected guide into a vector-specific plasmid workflow, and validate the resulting construct.
metadata.scope: Training/library SOP draft for Cas9 knockout-style sgRNA vector cloning. It uses Addgene planning and guide-design guidance and requires confirmation against the selected vector protocol, safety documentation, institutional approval, and local laboratory policy.
beforeYouBegin: Define the editing goal: knockout, HDR, base editing, prime editing, CRISPRi, or CRISPRa.
Confirm the PAM and guide length for the selected Cas enzyme and vector; do not reuse overhangs from another vector without checking the plasmid map.
Sequence or verify the genomic region in the working cell line if polymorphisms may affect guide binding.
Design at least two to four independent guides per target for biological confidence.

steps.action: Select the target region based on the biological goal; for knockout, prioritize constitutive early coding exons or essential protein domains.
Use gRNA design software to identify candidate guides with high predicted on-target activity and an acceptable off-target profile.

parameters.rawText: Design at least two to four independent guides per target for biological confidence.

steps.action: Exclude guides overlapping common variants, repeats, splice ambiguity, or unintended homologous sequences when possible.
Choose final guides and record genomic coordinate, strand, PAM, exon number, predicted score, and top off-target sites.
Design forward and reverse oligos with the exact vector-required overhangs and any required leading base for U6 or other promoter expression.
steps.criticalNotes: Do not reuse overhangs from another vector without checking the plasmid map.

steps.action: Order oligos and resuspend them in nuclease-free water or TE according to laboratory convention.
Anneal oligos using the vector-protocol-compatible buffer and thermal program.
Prepare the gRNA vector using the restriction-enzyme or Golden-Gate-style digestion/ligation workflow specified for that plasmid.
Combine the annealed oligo duplex with prepared vector and ligation or assembly reagents according to the vector-specific protocol.
Transform into competent E. coli, plate on the correct antibiotic, and incubate under conditions appropriate for the plasmid backbone.
Pick colonies, miniprep plasmid DNA, and verify the guide insert by Sanger sequencing using the vector primer.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Must confirm the correct guide sequence and orientation, with no mutation in the guide scaffold or flanking region.

steps.action: Archive the validated plasmid sequence, map, bacterial glycerol stock, and guide-design record.
steps.expectedResult: Validated construct and its documentation are archived.

controls.name: Edit-validation assay
controls.description: Plan before cell editing; validate by amplicon sequencing, Sanger/TIDE-style analysis, genotyping, protein loss, or phenotype as appropriate.

expectedOutputs: Guide-design record and final validation status.

troubleshooting.cause: Wrong overhangs, inactive ligase/enzyme, or poor competent cells.
troubleshooting.solution: Check the vector map, use fresh reagents, and include a transformation control.

troubleshooting.cause: Incomplete vector digestion or high background.
troubleshooting.solution: Gel-purify digested vector and use a negative control.

troubleshooting.cause: Weak guide, inaccessible locus, or poor delivery.
troubleshooting.solution: Test additional guides and verify Cas9/gRNA expression.
Use multiple independent guides and rescue or orthogonal validation.

safety: Wear lab coat, gloves, and eye protection; follow local biosafety, chemical-safety, and waste rules for the relevant materials.
For genome-editing or viral-vector workflows, confirm institutional approval, organism/cell-line restrictions, containment level, and waste decontamination before starting.
Use nuclease-free, contamination-controlled workflows and physically separate pre-PCR and post-PCR/library-amplification areas when possible.
